newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu attacks Palestinian Authority on police.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu attacks Palestinian Authority on police.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu lashed out on Sunday at the Palestinian Authority over the alleged involvement of PLO police in plans to attack Jewish settlers.
Calling for a "basic and immediate change in Palestinian Authority policy," Netanyahu told reporters the PA must "fight terrorism and turn (its) police against terror and not towards terror".
Earlier, officials said Palestinian security forces had detained several of their own police officers on Israeli accusations they planned to attack Jewish settlers.
"An investigative committee that formed two days ago is continuing its work to check the allegations against the members of the Palestinian police," the official Palestinian WAFA news agency said.
"Some members have been detained to question them about these allegations," it said. A spokesman for Palestinian President Yasser Arafat confirmed the report.
"I am sorry to say the problem of Palestinian policemen is one that has now reached into the top of the Palestinian police force," Netanyahu told reporters.

"Imagine what would have happened if there was evidence or concrete signs that the chief of Israel's police had sent policemen or soldiers to murder Palestinian children," Netanyahu said, drawing a parallel with a top PLO officer who Israeli officials have named in off-the-record remarks.
"There would have been a worldwide outcry," he said.
Israel had accused Palestinian police of carrying out a shooting attack that damaged the car of a rabbi in the West Bank a week and a half ago and planning other attacks on settlers.
Israeli officials demanded that Palestinian police arrest Deputy Commander Jihad Masouni, a senior official in the Nablus police they said had ordered the attack.
A spokesman for Arafat could not say if Masouni was under arrest or how many police officers were detained.
Israel arrested three Palestinian police officers last week, saying they were on their way to attack Har Bracha, a Jewish settlement near the Palestinian-ruled city of Nablus in the West Bank.
They also arrested another police officer on suspicion of planning attacks near the West Bank town of Tulkarm.
Palestinians have demanded the Israelis turn over the officers so they can interrogate them.

"The Palestinian police prisoners who are being held by the Israelis should be handed over to the Palestinian Authority for the continuation of the investigation," a spokesman for security forces told WAFA.
Palestinian police operate in parts of the West Bank and the Gaza Strip under Israel-PLO peace deals reached since 1993.

Security cooperation between Israeli and Palestinian troops outlined in the deals has broken down since a March deadlock with the Jewish state over the construction of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
